description: Command and content policy shared by every agent hook entrypoint. Blocking rules cover irreversible or credential-exposing actions only; everything judgement-dependent is a review-level warning so the guard never becomes the reason a normal task cannot proceed.

blockedCommands.reason: Recursive force-delete targeting the filesystem root or the home directory.
Recursive force-delete with an unquoted variable path; if the variable is empty this deletes the working directory or worse. Expand the path explicitly first.
Filesystem creation destroys everything on the target device.
Raw write to a block device.
Executing a downloaded script. Fetch it, read it, and get approval before running it.
World-writable permission on the filesystem root.
Force-push to a shared branch rewrites history other people already have. Ask the user; use --force-with-lease on a feature branch instead.
Deleting a remote repository is irreversible and remote.
Publishing is an externally visible release action and needs explicit user authorization.
This framework never modifies global Git configuration. Set repository-local config instead.
Blanket history rewriting; if a secret needs removing, do it deliberately with a reviewed plan.
Reading or uploading a credential file. Credentials must not enter logs, prompts, or network calls.
Bypassing hooks to force a commit through. Fix what the hook is complaining about.

reviewCommands.reason: Recursive delete: confirm the exact path.
Deletes untracked and ignored files irrecoverably.
Dependency change: confirm the dependency decision first (see the engineering-dependencies skill).
Outbound network fetch: confirm the destination is expected.
